key_insight: Clifford template compilation shows a sharp complexity split: some commuting Clifford inverse problems are efficiently solvable or even quantum-amenable, while small changes in exponent constraints make the problem NP-complete.
engineering_relevance: This matters for quantum compiler and fault-tolerant control design because it tells engineers when template-based synthesis/search can be done efficiently and when it may become intractable.
method: Analyze commuting Clifford templates as an inverse problem over Pauli transformations.
Classify feasibility and solution recovery under different exponent restrictions (unrestricted, binary, bounded total count).
Relate special cases to finite-field discrete logarithm, classical polynomial-time algorithms, and NP-completeness.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports formal complexity classifications across multiple template families, including membership in NP∩BQP, classical polynomial-time solvability for some self-inverse cases, and NP-completeness for several restricted variants.
watch_item: The favorable quantum/classical algorithms apply only to specific commuting or self-inverse structures, so real compiler instances may not inherit the same tractability.
paper_title: Computational Complexity of Clifford Template Compilation: Are Quantum Computers Useful for Compiling Quantum Circuits?
